S01.purpose: Defines who your business is and what it stands for — the identity statement your strategy, hiring, and investment decisions should all trace back to, so growth never drifts from the brand you built.
S01.driverContext: Identity Drivers govern this module most strongly — character, values, field, domain determine whether strategy is authentic or performed.

S02.purpose: Sets your strategic north star — comparing where leadership says the business is heading with where its decisions are actually taking it, so you course-correct before the gap widens.
S02.driverContext: Market Drivers and Identity Drivers interact here — the market pulls direction while identity anchors it.

S03.purpose: Tests your strategy for internal contradictions — flagging where goals, budgets, and initiatives work against each other before they cancel each other out in execution.
S03.driverContext: Cultural Drivers are critical here — coherence breaks when culture and strategy diverge.

S04.purpose: Checks that sales, operations, finance, and HR are executing the same strategy — surfacing the functions pulling in competing directions so you can realign them early.
S04.driverContext: All seven drivers converge in this module — convergence requires alignment of identity, market, culture, timing, and long-term forces simultaneously.

S05.purpose: Sets the rhythm of your strategy reviews and decision cycles — so plans are revisited when the market moves, not just when the annual offsite arrives.
S05.driverContext: Timing Drivers dominate here — the R-Series rhythm intelligence directly informs strategic timing quality.

S06.purpose: Tracks your strategy from vision to delivery — showing where initiatives stall between the boardroom and the front line, and which bottleneck to clear first.
S06.driverContext: Structural Drivers and Timing Drivers interact here — operational structures either enable or block strategic flow.

S07.purpose: Maps the environment your strategy operates in — the market conditions, constraints, and internal pressures shaping outcomes — so you plan for the field as it is, not as the slide deck assumed.
S07.driverContext: All seven drivers create the field simultaneously. The timing field (from R-Series) and long-term field are the most influential layers.

S08.purpose: Scores how much momentum your strategy actually has — which initiatives are accelerating, which are meeting resistance, and where pushing harder beats changing course.
S08.driverContext: Human Drivers create internal forces; Market Drivers create external forces; Timing Drivers govern executive force direction; Direction Drivers create the underlying gravitational pull.

S09.purpose: Ranks your strategic priorities by weight and urgency — so people stop treating everything as top priority and resources follow what matters most.
S09.driverContext: Identity Drivers create the most stable gravitational pull. Direction Drivers create the primary gravitational centre toward authentic future.

S10.purpose: Identifies the handful of focus areas where your effort compounds — and the initiatives that keep consuming budget without moving the business.
S10.driverContext: Cultural Drivers create the most persistent orbits — culture determines which cycles repeat. Timing Drivers govern orbital timing and frequency.

S11.purpose: Tracks how fast your organization notices and responds to market shifts — how long a trend takes to reach a decision, and whether the response holds or fades.
S11.driverContext: Every driver produces trend signals. Conflicts between Identity and Market signals are the most common cause of a stalled response.

S12.purpose: Projects where your current trajectory takes the business over the long term — showing whether your stated ambition is reachable from where you stand, and what has to change if it isn't.
S12.driverContext: Direction Drivers are primary here — origin, source, executive, and completeness encode the underlying horizon truth. The Timing Horizon (from R-Series) determines arrival timing.

R01.purpose: Maps your operating rhythm end to end — when decisions get made, when work ships, and how information flows — so timing is designed around market and customer signals rather than habit.
R01.driverContext: All seven drivers create rhythm patterns. Timing Drivers (from R-Series itself) and Identity Drivers create the most stable, coherent rhythm maps.

R02.purpose: Measures how fast work actually moves through your organization — where pace is building, where it's stalling, and whether your delivery speed matches what you've promised.
R02.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern velocity most directly. Identity Drivers determine the baseline rhythm pace. Market Drivers create external velocity pressures.

R03.purpose: Catches your delivery rhythm slipping — a little later each cycle — and flags it before the drift shows up in a missed quarter.
R03.driverContext: Cultural Drivers are the primary source of silent drift. Timing Drivers reveal the speed of drift. Identity Drivers determine whether drift is correctable or structural.

R04.purpose: Scores how well your operating rhythm holds up under pressure — disruption, volatility, surprise demand — so you know whether one bad week breaks the routine.
R04.driverContext: Identity Drivers create the underlying rhythm stability. Structural Drivers provide the operational scaffolding. Market Drivers are the primary source of destabilising shocks.

R05.purpose: Shows where workload is piling onto some teams while others have slack — so you rebalance before overload turns into burnout and attrition.
R05.driverContext: Human Drivers and Cultural Drivers create the most common imbalances. Identity Drivers set the equilibrium point. Direction Drivers reveal the ideal balance for the enterprise's future.

R06.purpose: Checks whether your teams' rhythms work together — where one team's cycle feeds another's queue, and where mismatched timing creates waiting.
R06.driverContext: Cultural Drivers generate the most powerful harmony conditions. Identity Drivers set how wide a range of cadences can coexist. Market Drivers are the most common source of disruption.

R07.purpose: Tests whether your organization runs on one coherent rhythm or many conflicting ones — the meeting, reporting, and delivery cycles that create noise when they clash.
R07.driverContext: Identity Drivers create the underlying coherence foundation. Cultural Drivers determine whether coherence is lived or stated. Timing Drivers reveal coherence quality over time.

R08.purpose: Shows how well the rhythms of your departments, systems, and teams knit into one operating cycle — and where the handoffs between them lose days.
R08.driverContext: Structural Drivers create the primary integration architecture. Timing Drivers determine integration timing. Identity Drivers determine whether integration is authentic or forced.

R09.purpose: Checks that your operating rhythm serves your strategy — flagging the cadences that keep teams busy but pull effort away from stated priorities.
R09.driverContext: Direction Drivers reveal the underlying alignment truth. Identity Drivers set the alignment baseline. Market Drivers test alignment under external conditions.

R10.purpose: Measures how close your teams are to a shared rhythm — which are converging on the same beat, and which are drifting apart.
R10.driverContext: All seven drivers contribute to convergence. Timing Drivers determine convergence timing. Direction Drivers set the convergence destination. Cultural Drivers are the most common convergence barrier.

R11.purpose: Measures how precisely your teams and systems are synchronised right now — the lag between them, and how long alignment lasts once achieved.
R11.driverContext: Timing Drivers are the primary synchronisation governors. Structural Drivers create the synchronisation architecture. Cultural Drivers determine whether synchronisation is sustained or sporadic.

R12.purpose: Tracks whether work moves through your operation without interruption — surfacing the pauses, handoffs, and rework loops that break flow.
R12.driverContext: Structural Drivers create the most common flow friction. Timing Drivers and Identity Drivers create the conditions for sustained flow.

R13.purpose: Scores how well your people's working rhythm matches the pace of your markets and culture — where the beat energises teams, and where it grinds them down.
R13.driverContext: Identity Drivers create the underlying alignment conditions. Direction Drivers reveal the alignment frequency the enterprise is naturally moving toward. Cultural Drivers determine whether alignment is felt and embodied.

R14.purpose: Monitors the heartbeat of your operation as it happens — the recurring delivery and decision cycles whose strength tells you the organisation's health, energy, and momentum.
R14.driverContext: Human Drivers generate the most visible pulse signals. Timing Drivers determine pulse regularity. Identity Drivers encode the natural pulse frequency of the enterprise.

R15.purpose: Profiles your organization's distinctive working rhythm — the timing fingerprint that sets it apart — so you protect what makes it fast and fix what makes it late.
R15.driverContext: Identity Drivers define the signature most profoundly. Cultural Drivers embed the signature into daily behaviour. Direction Drivers reveal whether the signature is evolving toward its highest expression.

R16.purpose: Reports the timing patterns your organization actually runs on — its true operating rhythm versus the schedule on paper.
R16.driverContext: Identity Drivers are primary at this layer. Timing Drivers provide the evidence base. Cultural Drivers determine whether rhythm identity is expressed or suppressed.

R17.purpose: Identifies what actually sets your organization's pace — the constraint, the person, or the process everything else waits on.
R17.driverContext: Identity and Direction Drivers together set the primary cadence. Cultural Drivers determine whether that cadence is visible or hidden. Market Drivers test character under pressure.

R18.purpose: Measures how well your operating rhythm fits your people and culture — where the pace is sustainable, and where it clashes with how your teams genuinely work.
R18.driverContext: Direction Drivers set which values matter most. Identity Drivers keep them grounded in what the organisation actually is. Cultural Drivers determine whether they show up in day-to-day work.

R19.purpose: Maps where your operating rhythm touches results — which timing choices move revenue, delivery, and morale, and which are just calendar habit.
R19.driverContext: All seven drivers simultaneously create and inhabit the rhythm field. Timing Drivers are the primary field generators. Direction Drivers define the field's ultimate direction.

R20.purpose: Shows one department's rhythm in full — its cycles, its bottlenecks, and its fit with the teams upstream and downstream of it.
R20.driverContext: Market Drivers define the external domain boundaries. Identity Drivers determine domain authority. Direction Drivers reveal whether the enterprise is growing, contracting, or transforming its domain.

R21.purpose: Rolls cadence up to business-unit level — comparing rhythm and reliability across units so you see which operating models to copy.
R21.driverContext: Direction Drivers define the business unit's outermost horizon. Identity Drivers determine business unit access. Cultural Drivers determine whether the enterprise can inhabit its full business unit.

R22.purpose: Puts the whole organization's rhythm on one screen — every unit's pace, drift, and sync — so leadership sees timing problems before they compound.
R22.driverContext: All seven drivers exist within the cadence landscape. Timing Drivers and Direction Drivers are the enterprise's guides through the larger rhythmic enterprise-wide view.

R23.purpose: Tracks how your operating rhythm changes across quarters and years — speeding up, slowing down, or quietly eroding.
R23.driverContext: Direction Drivers are primary at the long-range layer. Identity Drivers determine the enterprise's relationship with long-range time. Cultural Drivers determine whether long-range is embraced or feared.

R24.purpose: Keeps the history of your rhythm — so you can date exactly when delivery started slipping, and connect it to what changed.
R24.driverContext: Timing Drivers generate the continuum evidence. Identity Drivers provide the thread of continuity. Direction Drivers reveal the direction of the continuum's arc.

R25.purpose: Traces a broken rhythm to its root cause — the dependency, decision bottleneck, or overload behind the slippage, rather than the team it happens to show up in.
R25.driverContext: Identity Drivers carry the underlying origin information. Cultural Drivers determine whether origin patterns are preserved, evolved, or abandoned. Timing Drivers map origin patterns across time.

R26.purpose: Audits where your timing data comes from and how much to trust it — so cadence decisions rest on real signals, not anecdote.
R26.driverContext: Direction Drivers and Identity Drivers reveal the source most directly. Cultural Drivers determine whether the source is accessed and honoured. Timing Drivers reveal the source's expression over time.

R27.purpose: Finds the rhythm your organization performs best at — the pace that maximises output without tipping teams into overload — and shows how far you are from it.
R27.driverContext: Direction Drivers define the peak destination. Identity Drivers determine peak capacity. All seven drivers must be aligned for the enterprise to approach its rhythm peak.

R28.purpose: Puts your operating rhythm under management — who owns each cycle, what its standard is, and what happens when it breaks.
R28.driverContext: Identity Drivers are the foundation of governance. Direction Drivers provide executive direction. Market Drivers are the primary challenges to rhythm governance.

R29.purpose: The executive summary of your organization's rhythm — pace, drift, and risk in the few numbers a leadership meeting actually needs.
R29.driverContext: All seven drivers must be at executive level for R29 to register completion. Direction Drivers and Identity Drivers are the final determinants of executive achievement.

R30.purpose: The complete picture of your enterprise timing — how every rhythm rolls up, where the organisation beats in sync, and where it fights itself.
R30.driverContext: All seven drivers contribute equally to completeness. The absence of completeness in any driver creates a gap that undermines the whole.

C02.purpose: Scores how well work actually moves through your organisation — handoffs, bottlenecks, and where process breaks down under real load.
C02.driverContext: Structural Drivers determine whether process is actually followed. Timing Drivers reveal where handoffs stall. Human Drivers govern whether people work around the process or through it.

C03.purpose: The single-score read on CORE as a whole — decision quality, execution cadence and governance posture combined into one number before you go deep on any one of them.
C03.driverContext: All seven drivers contribute to this composite read. Direction Drivers set what 'coherent' means for this organisation. Identity Drivers determine how honestly the other three dimensions get scored.

C04.purpose: Rolls transformation pace and stability up into one executive read — is change actually landing, or just being announced.
C04.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern velocity. Cultural Drivers determine whether adoption is genuine or performed. Direction Drivers define what value the transformation was for in the first place.

C05.purpose: The executive view of delivery tempo across every team — where cadence holds, where it is drifting, and what that is costing.
C05.driverContext: Timing Drivers are the primary signal here. Structural Drivers determine whether teams can even keep the same rhythm. Direction Drivers set the tempo the organisation should be running at.

C06.purpose: Assesses how well your operating model — structure, decision rights, delivery rhythm — actually fits the strategy it is meant to carry.
C06.driverContext: Structural Drivers are the model itself. Direction Drivers define what the model has to be fit for. Identity Drivers determine how much resistance a redesign will meet.

C07.purpose: Checks whether strategy, priorities and the work actually being done are still the same thing, or have quietly diverged.
C07.driverContext: Direction Drivers set the strategy being aligned to. Structural Drivers determine whether resourcing actually follows it. Cultural Drivers govern how the strategy cascades below the top team.

C08.purpose: Scores the health of a change programme itself — sponsorship, adoption, resistance and sustainment — separately from whether the change was the right call.
C08.driverContext: Identity Drivers reveal how much sponsors are actually willing to spend on this. Cultural Drivers govern resistance. Timing Drivers determine whether the programme is sequenced to actually stick.

C09.purpose: One board-level score combining decision quality, delivery confidence, risk exposure and governance assurance — the number a director asks for before the detail.
C09.driverContext: All seven drivers roll up here. Direction Drivers set what the board should actually be worried about. Identity Drivers determine whether this reads as an honest score or a managed one.

Q01.purpose: Maps every significant decision in play across your organization — who owns each, what it blocks, and which ones actually deserve executive attention.
Q01.driverContext: Identity Drivers anchor the decision field. Direction Drivers reveal the highest-probability paths. All seven drivers simultaneously inhabit and shape the decision field.

Q02.purpose: Shows the live status of your decisions in progress — what's decided, what's stuck, and what's waiting on whom.
Q02.driverContext: Identity Drivers determine which decisions get taken up at all. Direction Drivers show which of them move the organisation toward its stated strategy. Every driver shapes the mix at once.

Q03.purpose: Simulates the paths a decision could take — playing your options forward so you see the second-order effects before committing.
Q03.driverContext: Direction Drivers clarify the stated strategy. Market Drivers expose which paths are viable. Identity Drivers determine which paths the enterprise can actually traverse.

Q04.purpose: Puts probabilities on outcomes — so your options are compared on likelihood-weighted value, not on whoever argued loudest.
Q04.driverContext: Market Drivers supply the most probability data. Direction Drivers reveal where probability and stated strategy converge. Timing Drivers govern when probability windows open and close.

Q05.purpose: Diagnoses whether now is the right time to decide — weighing the cost of deciding early against the cost of waiting.
Q05.driverContext: Timing Drivers carry the most weight in this module. The R-Series rhythm intelligence feeds directly into timing. Identity Drivers determine the enterprise's natural decision tempo.

Q06.purpose: Detects decisions and priorities working against each other — two teams solving opposite problems with the same budget.
Q06.driverContext: Cultural Drivers create the most persistent interference patterns. Identity Drivers and Market Drivers generate signals that can either constructively amplify or destructively cancel each other.

Q07.purpose: Checks new decisions against the ones you've already made — so today's call doesn't quietly reverse last quarter's.
Q07.driverContext: Identity Drivers create the foundation of coherence. Cultural Drivers determine whether coherence is maintained under pressure. Direction Drivers reveal the coherence ceiling the enterprise is capable of reaching.

Q08.purpose: Closes decisions properly — recorded rationale, a named owner, and a definition of done, so nothing gets relitigated at the next meeting.
Q08.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern commitment timing. Identity Drivers determine whether commitment is deliberate or forced. Direction Drivers reveal whether each commitment moves the enterprise toward or away from its stated strategy.

Q09.purpose: Structures the choice between options — criteria, weights, and scores in the open, so your selection survives scrutiny.
Q09.driverContext: Identity Drivers shape selection criteria at the underlying level. Market Drivers provide the external filter. Direction Drivers reveal which selections are aligned with the enterprise's highest path.

Q10.purpose: Weighs a decision across every factor at once — financial, operational, people, and risk — instead of the single lens it arrived in.
Q10.driverContext: Direction Drivers unlock the underlying decision dimensions. Identity Drivers determine which dimensions the enterprise is capable of perceiving and operating within.

Q11.purpose: Stress-tests a scenario against reality — the assumptions it needs to be true, and which of them your own data already contradicts.
Q11.driverContext: Market Drivers supply the most reality-grounding data. Identity Drivers determine reality tolerance. Direction Drivers reveal whether the enterprise is aligned with the reality of its authentic future.

Q12.purpose: Explores the full range of scenarios — best case, worst case, and the messy middle — with the consequences of each laid side by side.
Q12.driverContext: Direction Drivers expand the decision scope toward its intended scope. Market Drivers constrain it. Identity Drivers determine which parts of that scope the enterprise can access.

Q13.purpose: Traces a problem to its root cause — following the chain past the symptoms so your fix lands where the problem starts.
Q13.driverContext: Identity Drivers contain the underlying origin codes. Direction Drivers reveal whether decisions originate from authentic calling or external pressure. Cultural Drivers shape unconscious decision origins.

Q14.purpose: Validates the data behind a decision — where it came from, how fresh it is, and whether it can carry the weight you're about to put on it.
Q14.driverContext: All seven drivers contribute source intelligence. Market Drivers supply external source data. Identity and Direction Drivers supply internal source wisdom. Cultural Drivers filter and amplify certain sources over others.

Q15.purpose: Surfaces the early signals of trouble — the leading indicators that move weeks before your results do, while there's still time to act.
Q15.driverContext: Market Drivers generate the highest volume of signals. Identity Drivers determine which signals are attended to. Direction Drivers emit the most important signals — often the quietest and most easily missed.

Q16.purpose: Spots the decisions you keep making again — the same call resurfacing every quarter because it was never resolved at the root.
Q16.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern decision frequency most directly. Identity Drivers set the natural frequency baseline. Market Drivers force frequency acceleration or deceleration based on external pressure.

Q17.purpose: Scores how aligned your stakeholders really are on a decision — surfacing quiet dissent before it becomes slow execution.
Q17.driverContext: Identity Drivers create the underlying alignment frequency. Direction Drivers determine whether alignment is building toward authentic amplification. Cultural Drivers propagate or dampen alignment across the enterprise.

Q18.purpose: Checks that different teams facing the same question decide it the same way — so your customers get one answer, not four.
Q18.driverContext: Cultural Drivers produce the most cross-team conflict. Identity Drivers set the shared standard decisions are measured against. Market Drivers introduce outside pressure that can pull teams in different directions.

Q19.purpose: Adjusts assessments for the mood in the room — separating what your data says from how people feel about it.
Q19.driverContext: Identity Drivers set the natural decision tone. Cultural Drivers reinforce or distort tone. Direction Drivers emit a executive tone that the enterprise must learn to match in its own decisions.

Q20.purpose: Adds the context a decision is missing — market conditions, history, and constraints — so you decide with the full picture.
Q20.driverContext: Human Drivers create the richest texture data. Cultural Drivers determine texture propagation. Identity Drivers shape the underlying texture character that persists across decision types.

Q21.purpose: Builds reusable decision frameworks — so your recurring choices follow a tested structure instead of starting from scratch each time.
Q21.driverContext: Structural Drivers determine form frameworks. Identity Drivers shape authentic form character. Cultural Drivers determine how form is received. Direction Drivers reveal the ideal form for each decision level.

Q22.purpose: Maps how a complex decision breaks into parts — dependencies, sequence, and owners — before anyone commits to the whole.
Q22.driverContext: Structural Drivers are primary here. Identity Drivers determine whether structure is authentic to the enterprise. Cultural Drivers determine whether formal structure matches actual decision behaviour.

Q23.purpose: The control panel for how your organization decides — its frameworks, thresholds, and escalation paths in one place.
Q23.driverContext: All seven drivers contribute to the architecture. Structural Drivers provide the framework. Direction Drivers reveal the architecture the enterprise is meant to operate through. Identity Drivers determine architectural authenticity.

Q24.purpose: Tests whether your decision models still fit reality — and retires the ones the market has moved past.
Q24.driverContext: Identity Drivers encode design preferences. Cultural Drivers determine whether good design is valued. Direction Drivers reveal the design standards the enterprise must achieve to fulfil its purpose.

Q25.purpose: Detects the patterns in your decision history — the setups that consistently precede wins, and the ones that precede write-offs.
Q25.driverContext: Cultural Drivers create the most persistent patterns. Identity Drivers encode pattern origins. Timing Drivers reveal pattern timing and recurrence frequency. Direction Drivers show which patterns must be preserved and which must be broken.

Q26.purpose: Reports your organization's decision signature — how it characteristically decides: fast or slow, top-down or consensus, bold or safe.
Q26.driverContext: Identity Drivers are the primary signature creators. Cultural Drivers either reinforce or dilute the signature. Direction Drivers reveal the fullest expression of the enterprise's decision signature.

Q27.purpose: Profiles your individual decision-makers — their speed, their biases, their hit rate — so assignments match strengths.
Q27.driverContext: Identity Drivers carry the most weight in this module. Direction Drivers reveal the fullest decision identity the enterprise is called to embody. Cultural Drivers determine how identity is expressed through daily decision behaviour.

Q28.purpose: Maps the stakeholders around a decision — what each one cares about, and what each one needs in order to say yes.
Q28.driverContext: Identity Drivers create authentic persona. Market Drivers shape the perceived persona. Cultural Drivers determine the gap between authentic and performed decision persona.

Q29.purpose: Assigns clear roles on every decision — who decides, who's consulted, who's informed — so nothing dies of ambiguity.
Q29.driverContext: Structural Drivers define formal roles. Identity Drivers determine whether people inhabit their roles authentically. Cultural Drivers determine how roles are respected. Direction Drivers reveal the role architecture the enterprise needs for its future.

Q30.purpose: A library of your organization's standard decisions — the calls each unit routinely makes, with the playbook for each.
Q30.driverContext: Structural Drivers govern functional mechanics. Timing Drivers determine function speed and rhythm. Identity Drivers determine function character. Market Drivers test function under real-world conditions.

Q31.purpose: Plans your decision capacity — how many significant calls your leaders can make well per week, and what to delegate when the queue exceeds it.
Q31.driverContext: Human Drivers determine capacity most directly. Structural Drivers provide capacity scaffolding. Timing Drivers reveal capacity limits under sustained pressure. Direction Drivers reveal the capacity ceiling the enterprise must build toward.

Q32.purpose: Scores each team's ability to decide well without escalating — so autonomy is granted on evidence, not seniority.
Q32.driverContext: Human Drivers are primary — competence lives in people. Identity Drivers reveal the competence character of the enterprise. Direction Drivers identify the competence levels required for the enterprise's highest future.

Q33.purpose: Scores individual decision-making skill — judgment, speed, and calibration — so development targets the actual gap.
Q33.driverContext: Human Drivers carry skill data. Identity Drivers reveal natural skill affinity. Cultural Drivers determine which skills are valued and developed. Direction Drivers reveal the skill set the enterprise must master.

Q34.purpose: A library of proven decision techniques — pre-mortems, expected value, decision trees — matched to the situations each one fits.
Q34.driverContext: Structural Drivers define formal techniques. Identity Drivers shape preferred technique styles. Cultural Drivers determine which techniques are adopted versus resisted. Direction Drivers reveal the techniques needed for the enterprise's future decisions.

Q35.purpose: Selects the right method for the decision at hand — a reversible call gets an afternoon, a one-way door gets the full treatment.
Q35.driverContext: Identity Drivers determine method affinity. Cultural Drivers determine which methods are culturally endorsed. Structural Drivers provide the method infrastructure. Direction Drivers reveal the most effective method mix for the enterprise's future.

Q36.purpose: Tracks decisions through your process — where each one sits, how long each stage takes, and where they queue.
Q36.driverContext: Structural Drivers create formal process architecture. Timing Drivers govern process speed and rhythm. Cultural Drivers determine whether processes are followed. Identity Drivers determine whether processes reflect the enterprise's authentic decision character.

Q37.purpose: Automates the routine layer of your decision-making — routing, reminders, and approvals — so human judgment is spent only where it's needed.
Q37.driverContext: Structural Drivers create workflow architecture. Human Drivers determine workflow behaviour. Cultural Drivers determine compliance with designed workflows. Timing Drivers reveal workflow speed and delay patterns.

Q38.purpose: Runs decisions as an enterprise system — one pipeline with standards, visibility, and accountability from proposal to review.
Q38.driverContext: All seven drivers are system inputs. Structural Drivers provide the system architecture. Direction Drivers define the system's ultimate performance standard. Identity Drivers determine the system's character and operating philosophy.

Q39.purpose: Maps the network a decision travels through — which functions touch it, and where it slows down crossing boundaries.
Q39.driverContext: Human Drivers create network nodes. Cultural Drivers determine network quality and trust levels. Market Drivers connect the network to external intelligence. Direction Drivers reveal which network connections are strategically vital.

Q40.purpose: The overview of your entire decision ecosystem — volume, speed, quality, and risk across the organization.
Q40.driverContext: Market Drivers provide the richest ecosystem intelligence. Timing Drivers determine ecosystem dynamics and change velocity. Direction Drivers reveal the ecosystem the enterprise must build to fulfil its purpose.

Q41.purpose: Summarises your decision intelligence — what's improving, what's degrading, and the three findings your leadership should act on.
Q41.driverContext: All seven drivers generate intelligence. Direction Drivers produce the highest-value but most often ignored intelligence. Identity Drivers determine intelligence appetite and processing style.

Q42.purpose: Indexes how much your organization actually learns from its decisions — whether insight accumulates, or evaporates between quarters.
Q42.driverContext: Identity Drivers determine awareness baseline. Direction Drivers represent the highest awareness the enterprise is called to operate from. Cultural Drivers either expand or suppress decision awareness across the organisation.

Q43.purpose: Monitors the risk sitting inside your pending decisions — concentration, exposure, and the calls nobody has stress-tested.
Q43.driverContext: Identity Drivers create self-awareness. Market Drivers generate environmental awareness. Cultural Drivers determine awareness spread across the organisation. Direction Drivers reveal the awareness dimensions the enterprise has not yet developed.

Q44.purpose: Scores one decision against the six requirements of decision quality — frame, alternatives, information, criteria, reasoning and commitment — and holds it to a bar set by how consequential and how reversible it is. Quality is the weakest link, not the average.
Q44.driverContext: Identity Drivers create fundamental clarity character. Cultural Drivers determine whether clarity is valued and expected. Timing Drivers reveal how clarity changes under time pressure. Direction Drivers emit the clearest possible signal for each major decision.

Q45.purpose: Turns your decision data into strategic insight — the patterns across many calls that point to what the business should do next.
Q45.driverContext: Direction Drivers produce the underlying insight. Identity Drivers determine insight capacity. Cultural Drivers either cultivate or suppress insight as an organisational capability. Timing Drivers reveal insight windows that open and close.

Q46.purpose: Shows you the consequences, scenarios, and futures of a decision before they arrive — so you commit with foresight rather than hindsight.
Q46.driverContext: Timing Drivers provide the most foresight data. Direction Drivers reveal the ultimate future toward which decisions should be oriented. Identity Drivers determine foresight character — bold or cautious, expansive or narrow.

Q47.purpose: Plans decisions against the long horizon — testing today's choices for whether the business you want in ten years can live with them.
Q47.driverContext: Direction Drivers carry the most weight in this module. Identity Drivers anchor the vision in what the organisation actually is. Cultural Drivers determine whether the vision shows up in daily decisions. Market Drivers test whether vision is grounded in viable reality.

Q48.purpose: Shows one decision through every stakeholder's eyes — customers, staff, owners, regulators — before you finalise it.
Q48.driverContext: Human Drivers carry perspective diversity. Cultural Drivers determine which perspectives are admitted or excluded. Identity Drivers shape the dominant perspective lens. Direction Drivers require perspectives that haven't yet been considered.

Q49.purpose: Explains the why behind a decision in plain language — so your people execute with conviction instead of compliance.
Q49.driverContext: All seven drivers contribute to understanding. Identity Drivers provide the interpretive framework. Direction Drivers reveal the understanding that is still missing. Cultural Drivers determine how deeply understanding is shared across the organisation.

Q50.purpose: Benchmarks your decision-making against best practice — where you're world-class, and where you're guessing.
Q50.driverContext: All seven drivers must be at a consistently high standard for Q50 to register completion. The Direction Driver is the final gate — mastery without long-term alignment is expertise, not governance.

Q51.purpose: Scores who actually influences your decisions — the informal network behind the org chart — so you know whose alignment matters.
Q51.driverContext: Identity Drivers create foundational decision power. Direction Drivers reveal the full power the enterprise is authorised to exercise. Cultural Drivers either amplify or drain decision power as it moves through the organisation.

Q52.purpose: Measures how strongly a decision lands — whether it changed behaviour on the ground, or just changed a slide.
Q52.driverContext: All seven drivers generate force. Market Drivers create the most visible external forces. Identity Drivers create the most durable internal forces. Direction Drivers generate the most powerful pull toward authentic outcomes.

Q53.purpose: Monitors your teams' capacity against their workload — who has room, who's saturated, and what that means for what you're about to commit.
Q53.driverContext: Human Drivers carry the most visible decision energy. Identity Drivers determine the baseline energy character. Cultural Drivers amplify or suppress energy. Direction Drivers emit an energy frequency that aligns decisions toward the enterprise's highest output.

Q54.purpose: Tracks whether decisions gain or lose momentum after they're made — the follow-through gap between deciding and doing.
Q54.driverContext: Timing Drivers reveal momentum trajectories. Identity Drivers determine the momentum character — bold or cautious. Cultural Drivers determine whether momentum is celebrated and protected or inadvertently broken.

Q55.purpose: Indexes how fast your organization decides — cycle time from question to call, benchmarked by decision type.
Q55.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern velocity most directly. Market Drivers set external velocity requirements. Identity Drivers determine comfort with pace. Direction Drivers reveal the velocity required to reach the enterprise's authentic future in time.

Q56.purpose: Plans how to decide faster without deciding worse — the approvals to remove, the data to pre-stage, the thresholds to delegate.
Q56.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern acceleration dynamics. Market Drivers create external acceleration pressure. Identity Drivers determine the enterprise's acceleration tolerance. Direction Drivers reveal whether the current acceleration rate is moving toward or away from the authentic future.

Q57.purpose: Estimates the business impact of a decision in money and time — so options are compared in the units your board uses.
Q57.driverContext: All seven drivers shape impact. Market Drivers provide the most immediate impact feedback. Identity Drivers determine impact character — transformational versus incremental. Direction Drivers reveal whether impact is building toward the enterprise's highest purpose.

Q58.purpose: Reports realised impact after the fact — what a decision actually delivered against what was claimed for it.

P11.driverContext: Identity Drivers define the excellence ceiling the enterprise can reach. Cultural Drivers determine whether excellence is a cultural expectation. Direction Drivers reveal the excellence standard required for the enterprise's highest future.

P12.purpose: Measures what's actually delivered — completed, shipped, in customers' hands — not what's in progress.
P12.driverContext: Structural Drivers create delivery infrastructure. Timing Drivers govern delivery timing. Human Drivers determine delivery quality. Market Drivers set delivery expectations. Cultural Drivers determine whether delivery commitments are non-negotiable.

P13.purpose: Assesses your execution discipline — whether plans convert into finished work at a predictable rate.
P13.driverContext: Structural Drivers create execution infrastructure. Human Drivers carry execution capability. Cultural Drivers determine execution discipline. Timing Drivers govern execution pacing. Direction Drivers reveal the execution standard required for transformational outcomes.

P14.purpose: Finds your highest-leverage productivity fixes — the constraint to lift first, ranked by impact rather than noise.
P14.driverContext: Structural Drivers provide the optimisation landscape. Timing Drivers reveal the optimal timing for each improvement initiative. Identity Drivers determine which optimisations are authentic to the enterprise's character.

P15.purpose: Turns your productivity data into decisions — the patterns across teams and time that say what to change next.
P15.driverContext: All seven drivers generate productivity intelligence. Structural Drivers create intelligence infrastructure. Cultural Drivers determine how intelligence is used. Direction Drivers reveal the intelligence the enterprise needs but has not yet developed.

P16.purpose: Measures productivity at team level — output, load, and blockers for each of your teams, in one comparable view.
P16.driverContext: Human Drivers are primary here — teams are made of people. Cultural Drivers determine team norms and collaboration quality. Structural Drivers provide team architecture. Identity Drivers determine team character.

P17.purpose: Assesses how well your people collaborate across boundaries — where teamwork multiplies output, and where handoffs subtract from it.
P17.driverContext: Cultural Drivers determine collaboration norms and quality. Human Drivers create collaboration capability. Structural Drivers provide collaboration infrastructure. Identity Drivers determine the enterprise's natural collaboration style.

P18.purpose: Assesses how well information moves through your organization — who's out of the loop, and what it costs you.
P18.driverContext: Human Drivers carry communication capability. Cultural Drivers determine communication norms. Structural Drivers create communication channels. Identity Drivers shape communication character — transparent, guarded, empowering, or controlling.

P19.purpose: Measures how engaged your people are in the work itself — the discretionary effort that never shows up on a timesheet.
P19.driverContext: Human Drivers carry engagement data. Cultural Drivers determine engagement conditions. Identity Drivers shape what the enterprise stands for — the primary engagement source. Direction Drivers reveal the engagement level required for the enterprise's transformational future.

P20.purpose: Assesses whether your teams have the skills the work demands — and where capability gaps are masquerading as performance problems.
P20.driverContext: Human Drivers carry capability data. Structural Drivers provide capability infrastructure. Identity Drivers determine capability character. Direction Drivers reveal the capability set required for the enterprise's highest performance future.

P21.purpose: Examines your core processes step by step — removing the approvals, waits, and workarounds that add time but not value.
P21.driverContext: Structural Drivers are primary here. Timing Drivers reveal process speed and flow issues. Cultural Drivers determine whether process improvement is valued. Human Drivers identify where process and people are mismatched.

P22.purpose: Analyses your workflows end to end — where each one stalls, loops, or gets reworked — so redesign targets facts.
P22.driverContext: Structural Drivers create workflow architecture. Human Drivers execute workflows. Cultural Drivers determine workflow discipline. Timing Drivers reveal workflow pacing and cadence issues.

P23.purpose: Measures whether your systems help or hinder output — the tools that save hours, and the ones that quietly consume them.
P23.driverContext: Structural Drivers are primary — systems are structural assets. Timing Drivers reveal system performance over time. Human Drivers determine system adoption quality. Market Drivers set system capability benchmarks.

P24.purpose: Assesses the productivity return on your technology — what each platform contributes against what it costs to run and maintain.
P24.driverContext: Structural Drivers govern technology infrastructure. Human Drivers determine technology adoption. Market Drivers set technology requirements. Timing Drivers reveal technology productivity trajectories and adoption timelines.

P25.purpose: Measures the yield of your innovation effort — ideas that reached the market against ideas that consumed budget.
P25.driverContext: Identity Drivers fuel authentic innovation. Market Drivers reveal innovation opportunities and threats. Cultural Drivers determine innovation appetite and risk tolerance. Direction Drivers reveal the innovation the enterprise must pursue to fulfil its purpose.

P26.purpose: Assesses productivity through transformation — keeping delivery standing while the organization changes underneath it.
P26.driverContext: Identity Drivers determine transformation character. Direction Drivers reveal the transformation the enterprise must make. Cultural Drivers determine transformation adoption. Structural Drivers provide the transformation infrastructure.

P27.purpose: Measures how your organization absorbs change — how fast teams return to full output after each reorganisation, tool, or process shift.
P27.driverContext: Cultural Drivers determine change receptivity — the most critical change variable. Identity Drivers determine change character. Structural Drivers provide change infrastructure. Timing Drivers govern change sequencing and pacing.

P28.purpose: Tracks whether your teams' ways of working are converging on shared standards — or fragmenting into local habits.
P28.driverContext: All seven drivers must converge simultaneously for enterprise productivity to reach its peak potential. Divergence in any driver creates fragmented output.

P29.purpose: Measures how tightly work across your teams is synchronised — so dependent tasks arrive together instead of waiting on each other.
P29.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern synchronisation most directly. Structural Drivers create the synchronisation architecture. Cultural Drivers determine synchronisation discipline. All seven drivers must synchronise simultaneously for peak enterprise productivity.

P30.purpose: Assesses your operation against flow — every system, team, and process moving without friction — and what stands between you and it.
P30.driverContext: All seven drivers must achieve flow simultaneously. The P-Series reaches P30 Flow when all prior modules (P01-P29) have been addressed. Flow is the natural result of resolved productivity intelligence.

F01.purpose: Gives you real-time clarity across your finances — revenue, cost, cash, and margin in one live view, instead of a month-end surprise.
F01.driverContext: Financial visibility is governed by Structural Drivers (systems, processes, reporting architecture) and Identity Drivers (what the enterprise believes about its own financial position). Timing Drivers determine how current the financial truth is.

G02.purpose: Surfaces market openings while they are still open — scored on how early, how credible, and how ready you are to act on them.
G02.driverContext: Market Drivers generate the raw signal. Timing Drivers determine whether it is caught early enough to matter. Direction Drivers decide whether the organisation is even looking for this kind of opportunity.

G03.purpose: Scores which growth paths are genuinely open to you against your actual capacity, not just which look attractive on a slide.
G03.driverContext: Direction Drivers narrow the field of real options. Structural Drivers determine which paths your capacity can actually carry. Market Drivers reveal how exposed each path is to competitive response.

G04.purpose: Assesses how ready your systems, processes and people are for the modernisation route you are considering — before you commit budget to it.
G04.driverContext: Structural Drivers determine technical readiness. Cultural Drivers govern organisational readiness. Timing Drivers reveal how much change capacity actually exists right now versus on paper.

G05.purpose: Scores how good your read on the market actually is — current, sourced and acted on, versus assumed.
G05.driverContext: Market Drivers are the direct subject. Timing Drivers reveal how stale the intelligence has become. Direction Drivers determine whether it is actually informing decisions or just being collected.

G06.purpose: Scores how far digital capability has actually reached — not the roadmap, the operating reality — across strategy, infrastructure, people and the customer experience it produces.
G06.driverContext: Direction Drivers set the digital strategy the organisation is converging toward. Structural Drivers determine whether infrastructure and process can carry that strategy. Cultural Drivers govern how readily people adopt new digital ways of working. Market Drivers reveal how the customer experiences the result.

G07.purpose: Checks whether the growth plan you are about to sign off is one your people, cash and operating rhythm can actually carry.
G07.driverContext: Direction Drivers set the ambition. Structural Drivers determine whether capacity can carry it. Timing Drivers reveal whether the milestones in the plan are sequenced realistically.

G08.purpose: The working view for running an advisory engagement against live growth data — how well the engagement's guidance is actually landing.
G08.driverContext: Direction Drivers reveal whether the advice matches the client's real strategy. Human Drivers govern whether the client actually adopts it. Timing Drivers determine how fast impact shows up.

G09.purpose: One board-ready score for growth performance — signal quality, plan execution and realised value combined.
G09.driverContext: All drivers roll up here. Direction Drivers set what 'good growth' means for this board. Market Drivers determine how much of the pipeline is real versus optimistic.

F02.purpose: Replaces guesswork in your numbers — budgets, forecasts, cash-flow projections and margin models that make your financial future predictable.
F02.driverContext: Timing Drivers govern forecasting quality — the enterprise's relationship with time determines how far ahead it can see with accuracy. Identity Drivers set the budgeting discipline baseline. Market Drivers introduce the variables that test scenario planning.

F03.purpose: Links your financial KPIs to what drives them — so when a number moves, you know which operational lever moved it.
F03.driverContext: All four business units (CORE, GROW, TALENT, FINANCE) feed KPI intelligence. Identity Drivers determine which KPIs the enterprise genuinely tracks vs. performs. Market Drivers create the external KPI pressure points.

F04.purpose: Spots waste, cost leakage, and productivity gaps across your business — improving margin without cutting capability.
F04.driverContext: Structural Drivers create the conditions where cost leakage hides — in processes, systems, and operational structures. Cultural Drivers determine whether cost discipline is behavioural or episodic. Identity Drivers set the tolerance for inefficiency.

F05.purpose: Measures and grows what your business is worth — the value drivers behind the number your owners and board care about most.
F05.driverContext: Direction Drivers carry the most weight in this module — they encode the ultimate financial trajectory of the enterprise. Identity Drivers determine whether the enterprise is building genuine value or performing valuation metrics. Market Drivers set the external multiplier environment.

F06.purpose: Assesses your financial governance — controls, approvals, and traceability strong enough to survive an audit or a due-diligence room.
F06.driverContext: Cultural Drivers determine whether governance becomes behavioural. Structural Drivers create the systems that enforce governance. Identity Drivers determine whether governance is authentic or performative.

F07.purpose: Assesses your finance function's readiness to lead — from bookkeeping and reporting to the forward-looking intelligence a CFO's office should produce.
F07.driverContext: Identity Drivers determine the CFO's authentic financial leadership capacity. Human Drivers govern the capability development trajectory. Cultural Drivers determine whether financial leadership is celebrated or sidelined.
